title: fix(plugin-list): ListView's columns-only fallback stops reading undeclared relational keys off a list column
body:
Fixes #7531
Clause-②: no

## What changed

Until the object definition loads, `ListView` builds its filter and sort candidates from the view's declared `columns` (the `!objectDef?.fields` branch of the `candidateFields` memo). That branch read `f.reference_to || f.reference`, `f.display_field || f.reference_field` and `f.id_field` off each column, and `ListColumnSchema` declares none of them in either casing. The card's ruling (comment 5809501335, letter **remove**) takes the three reads out. The fallback candidate now carries only what a column declares. The relational target arrives with the object definition through the `objectDef.fields` branch, which this PR leaves untouched.

- `packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx`: removes the three properties. The objectui#7642 census comment above them becomes one line that points at this card. Nothing else in the file changes.
- `packages/plugin-list/src/__tests__/ListView.columnsOnlyRelationalReads-7531.test.tsx`: the pin and its two lit controls.
- `.changeset/7531-listview-column-undeclared-reads.md`: `patch` on `@object-ui/plugin-list`.

## Stop condition: the producer census (run before deleting)

**Method.** The census was an AST walk. The file list and the file contents both came from the same git ref (`git ls-tree -r` and `git cat-file --batch`), never from a worktree:
- objectui at `6881e9e47` (this branch's base).
- The sibling objectstack at `bc80e1626` (its `origin/main` when this ran).

The walk parsed these kinds of file:
- `.ts .tsx .js .jsx .mjs .cjs .mts .cts`, using the TypeScript compiler API;
- `.json` and `.yaml`, parsed whole;
- fenced `json` / `yaml` / `ts` / `js` blocks inside `.md` / `.mdx`.

**What counted as a column object.** An object literal that is an element of an array bound to any of:
- a `columns` property;
- a `columns` JSX attribute;
- a `columns = [...]` assignment;
- a variable named like `cols` / `columns`, or typed with a `Column` type.

The census looked for eight spellings on those objects: `reference_to`, `reference`, `display_field`, `reference_field`, `id_field`, `referenceTo`, `displayField` and `idField`. It also listed two wider shapes:
- Any object literal that carries `field` plus one of the eight, wherever it sits. This catches columns built by a `map`.
- Any non-test object literal that carries `field` plus a spread. This catches keys that could arrive at runtime.

**Controls.**
- Population control: known column keys must hit in the same walk. `field` hit 460 column objects in objectui and 435 in objectstack. `width` hit 27 in objectui and 41 in objectstack. The walk found 956 column objects in objectui and 515 in objectstack.
- Detector control: a throwaway repo with one column carrying a target key in each carrier. The carriers were a TS property, a JSX `columns` attribute, a `cols` variable, JSON, YAML, a Markdown json block and a Markdown ts block. The walk hit 7 of 7.

**Results**

| repo | column objects carrying one of the eight | what they are |
|---|---|---|
| objectstack `bc80e1626` | 0 | none |
| objectui `6881e9e47` | 4 | 3 line-item grid columns, 1 grid-view test fixture |

- `apps/console/src/dev/DevLookup.tsx`, `docs/adr/0001-master-detail-subform.md` (the `record:line_items` example) and `packages/fields/src/widgets/GridField.test.tsx` are **line-item grid columns** (`GridField` / `LineItemsField`). That is a different contract: its columns are shaped like field defs, and `GridField` reads `c.reference`, `c.displayField` and `c.idField` off them on purpose. They are not list columns.
- `packages/plugin-grid/src/__tests__/ObjectGrid.linkCellAnchor.test.tsx` is **a grid-view column carrying `reference_to: 'crm_account'`**. That makes it the one list-column hit. It is classified as **not a producer**, for three reasons:
  - It is an inline input to a unit test that renders `ObjectGrid` directly, so `ListView`'s fallback never sees it.
  - No `ObjectGrid` code reads a relational key off a column. The lookup cell takes its target from the object definition's field, through `applyRelationalMeta(fieldMeta, objectDefField)`.
  - The fixture supplies no object definition, so the key reaches nothing, with or without this PR.

  ⚠️ If the stop condition is meant to count any fixture, this PR should be closed. See the note at the end of this body.
- None of the wider shapes found a list-column producer. The `field` plus relational key matches were form section fields, action and bulk-action params, a form field schema and an engine log record. The spread matches (including the 8 spread column literals in objectui) carry none of the eight spellings.
- **Not measured: `objectstack-ai/cloud`.** That repo cannot be read from this container. It was not censused, and this PR makes no claim about it.

## Downstream readers of the three keys (measured)

- **Sort:** the `sortFields` memo reads only `value`, `label` and `type` from each candidate. It never read the three keys, so sorting is unaffected.
- **Filter:** `FilterBuilder` draws its remote `LookupValuePicker` only when the field is lookup-like, has no static option domain, and has a `referenceTo` (or `type === "user"`). The picker then reads `displayField` (default `"name"`) and `idField` (default `"id"`).
- **Spec-shaped columns see no change.** A column that `ListColumnSchema` parses cannot carry any of the five read spellings (the pin's first case asserts this against the installed spec). So all three values were already `undefined` for such a column. The plain-column control stays green with the reads put back (see the ablation below). Once the definition loads, the `objectDef.fields` branch supplies `referenceTo`. The third case asserts this, and it passes with and without the reads.

## Pin, and the ablation that proves it can fail

The pin holds `getObjectSchema` pending on purpose, so the columns-only branch is the only one that runs. It captures the candidate list `ListView` hands to `FilterBuilder`, using a `vi.mock` that inherits the real module and overrides only `FilterBuilder`. The four cases:
1. The spec refuses each of the five spellings on a column (`unrecognized_keys`). Control: the bare column parses.
2. **Control:** a plain column gives the columns-only candidate list (`account_id` / `Account` / `lookup`, then `name` / `Name` / `text`), with no `referenceTo`.
3. **Pin:** a column carrying the five keys gives a candidate list that `toStrictEqual`s the plain one, with `referenceTo`, `displayField` and `idField` all undefined.
4. **Control:** when the definition resolves with `reference: 'crm_account'`, the candidate shows `referenceTo: 'crm_account'`. This proves the capture sees the key when one exists.

**Ablation, on HEAD `086e71456`.** The three reads were put back with `node ../objectstack/scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode, holding the verify lock:
- Mutation on disk: anchor count 1 → 0; `ListView.tsx` blob `03798ad2b3be` → `39feb0e2facd`; count of the restored read line in the file = 1.
- Result: `Tests  1 failed | 3 passed (4)`. Only the pin went red:
  ```
  -     "displayField": undefined,
  -     "idField": undefined,
  +     "displayField": "name",
  +     "idField": "id",
  -     "referenceTo": undefined,
  +     "referenceTo": "account",
  ```
- Restore: blob after restore `03798ad2b3be` equals the HEAD blob, and `git diff HEAD` on the file is empty.
- Resolution path: the test imports `../ListView` (source), so the mutated file is what ran. No `dist/` is in that path, so no rebuild was needed for either leg.
- The first attempt did nothing: the tool refused it because the replacement text still contained the anchor, so the anchor count could not drop. No test ran, and the tool restored and verified the file. The run above is the second attempt, with a corrected anchor.

## Verification (HEAD `086e71456`)

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-list/` from the repo root: `Test Files  93 passed (93)`, `Tests  1098 passed (1098)`.
- `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '@object-ui/plugin-list^...' build` (12 packages built; `Scope: 13 of 47`), then `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-list type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`): exit 0. `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` includes the new test.
- `pnpm check:control-bytes`: OK.
- `pnpm check:new-line-citations`: 0 new citations.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`: ✅, one changeset declared.
- `pnpm check:changeset-claims`: 7 pending changesets name `ListView.tsx`. All were read. They cover gantt, kanban, `userActions` and sort-comment changes, none describes the candidate fallback's relational reads, and all stay true.
- These gates all exit 0: vi.mock inherit / specifiers / override-shape, `check-test-path-roots`, changeset fixed / no-major / overwrite, `check:spec-symbols`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:phantom-deps`, `check-type-check-coverage` and `check-lint-coverage`.
- eslint on the touched files:
  - `ListView.tsx`: 0 errors and 183 warnings, with per-rule counts identical to the base file (checked through `--stdin` at the same path).
  - The new test: 0 errors and 0 warnings.
  - `eslint.config.js` has no type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project` or `projectService`), so this diff cannot change the verdict on any file it did not touch. The full `pnpm lint` is left to CI.

## Acceptance notes

- **Stop condition, and one call for the reviewer.** The ruling says to stop if a producer puts one of these keys on a list column. The census found no producer. It did find one list-column fixture: the plugin-grid test above. I read that fixture as not a producer, for the reasons given in the census section. If the ruling is meant to count any fixture, close this PR. The fix is then either to drop the inert key from that fixture or to rule it out explicitly, and removing the reads becomes a fresh dispatch.
- **A comment made stale here and left alone on purpose.** The `objectDef.fields` branch's comment still says "The SIBLING branch above (the `schema.columns` fallback) is NOT narrowed … That is a different question and is filed, not answered here." After this PR the sibling reads none of those keys. The dispatch fenced every other line of `ListView.tsx`, so that comment is untouched. The `domain:ui` seat's planned same-file docblock edits (after objectui#10534 lands) are the natural place to cut it.
- **Inert fixture key, not filed.** In `ObjectGrid.linkCellAnchor.test.tsx`, the case "a lookup column pointing at ANOTHER object stays plain" passes no matter what the column carries. The column's `reference_to` is read by nothing, and the fixture has no object definition. This is a test-quality note, and it has no carrier.
- **Two out-of-scope findings are reported to the seat for filing** (neither is changed here):
  - The `objectDef.fields` branch reads `display_field` / `reference_field` / `id_field`, but not the spec's `displayField`. A probe showed that a definition field carrying only `displayField` gives a candidate with no `displayField`.
  - The columns-only fallback also reads `f.options`, which `ListColumnSchema` refuses.
